subject: Planned safety rotation for inference nodes — WestUS1
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>
To: Priya Desai <ops@acmecloud.com>, Tom Nguyen <support@nubex.ai>, Sophie Martin <sophie@brightbank.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Planned safety rotation for inference nodes — WestUS1

Hi all,

We wanted to give advance notice of a planned, rolling safety rotation of inference nodes in the WestUS1 region. This is a preventative maintenance operation: we will cycle driver and firmware versions on a subset of nodes to address a latent compatibility issue discovered during routine validation.

Window: Tue, Dec 1 — Wed, Dec 2, 2026
Staged cadence: 2-hour windows per node pool (non-overlapping by AZ)
Expected customer impact: transient 1–2s p99 spikes for affected allocations; degraded throughput for <5 minutes during an individual pool rotation. No scheduled full-region outage.

Mitigations we will apply:
- Canary the first pool at the start of the window, with health checks and automatic rollback
- Route traffic away from updated pools until KV caches warm (prefetch disabled for canary)
- Bump autoscaling headroom and enable fallback to warm model variants for critical routes

We've attached the checklist and the planned node-by-node timeline. If you have strict latency SLAs or pinned capacity that cannot tolerate even short spikes, reply and we'll work with you to either delay the window for your tenancy or provide a dedicated maintenance-safe routing policy.

Attachments: maintenance-checklist-v1.2.pdf, westus1-rotation-timeline.csv

Thanks,
Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Head of Reliability Communications, Redwood Inference

From: Priya Desai <ops@acmecloud.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Nguyen <support@nubex.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Planned safety rotation for inference nodes — WestUS1

Thanks for the heads-up, Hannah. A couple quick questions:

1) Our workloads rely heavily on prefix caching (persistent KV caches). Will caches be preserved across the rotation, or should we expect cache misses for ~10–20 minutes?
2) Can you confirm which AZs are in the first wave? We have a small fallback pool in us-west-1 that we can divert to if AZ1 is impacted.

If needed we can take the affected traffic to our fallback pool, but would prefer Redwood to manage routing automatically.

—Priya
Priya Desai
SRE Lead, Acme Cloud

From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 11:08:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Planned safety rotation for inference nodes — WestUS1

Hannah — internal note on Priya's questions and our plan:

1) KV cache behavior: caches will be dropped on the rotated nodes (we're replacing driver + firmware). We will keep a short-lived shadow warm pool of compatible instances to absorb traffic for 10–15 minutes while caches rehydrate. Please confirm that "shadow warm pool" is reflected in the public note (I added the line about routing away from updated pools, but be explicit about 10–15 minutes).

2) Wave 1 AZs: az-westus1a and az-westus1b. Wave 2: az-westus1c.

3) Rollback: automatic rollback if 5xx rate increases by >0.5% sustained for 3 minutes. We'll also hold the canary for manual inspection if latency exceeds 99th percentile baseline by >2s.

I'll join the customer thread if you want me to chime in on the technical details.

- Marcus
Senior Platform Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>
To: Priya Desai <ops@acmecloud.com>, Tom Nguyen <support@nubex.ai>, Sophie Martin <sophie@brightbank.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 02 Dec 2026 13:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Planned safety rotation for inference nodes — WestUS1 (completed)

Hi Priya / Tom / Sophie,

Quick status update: the scheduled rotation in WestUS1 is complete. Summary:
- Start: 2026-12-01 02:00 UTC (canary pools)
- Completed: 2026-12-02 21:40 UTC
- Impact observed: transient p99 latency spikes (1–3s) during pool transitions; one canary required a rollback at 2026-12-01 03:05 UTC and was postponed for manual inspection, then successfully rotated later in Wave 2.

What we did for customers:
- Routed traffic to shadow warm pools for ~12 minutes per rotated pool to reduce cache-thrashing impact.
- Automatically retried idempotent requests from the edge for 30s during pool transition windows.
- No customer data exposure or rollback-required corruption observed.

If you noticed elevated latency beyond what we describe here, please send timestamps and sample request IDs and we'll correlate against our traces.

Thanks for your patience. I'll follow up with the post-maintenance notes and remediation items (including a minor automation action to reduce the canary sensitivity threshold).

Hannah

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 03 Dec 2026 16:03:00 -0800
Subject: Post-maintenance recap & actions — WestUS1 rotation

Team — brief postmortem summary to add to INF-4729 and the runbook:

Timeline highlights:
- 2026-12-01 02:00 UTC: Canary Wave 1 — initial driver/firmware applied to az-westus1a; observed 1.8s p99 jump for ~45s, auto-rollback triggered at 03:05 UTC due to 5xx spike on canary (root cause: edge retry storm against the newly rotated instances).
- 2026-12-01 03:20 UTC: Manual investigation; increased client-side retry backoff and re-applied to canary successfully at 03:55 UTC.
- 2026-12-02 08:10 UTC: Progressed waves 2–4; overall completion 2026-12-02 21:40 UTC.

Action items (owners):
- Reduce default edge retry aggressiveness for rollouts (Dylan) — due 2026-12-10
- Add an automated warm-pool creation step as part of rotation playbook (Marcus) — due 2026-12-08
- Update customer notice template to include explicit warm-pool expectation (Hannah) — due 2026-12-04

Notes: the attached checklist got a minor revision during the run; I'm attaching the updated checklist to INF-4729 and the Drive folder. No additional customer credits are required; we offered outreach to any tenant that reports >5% sustained error rate, and no tenants met that threshold.

- Hannah
